summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted for evaluation of worsening shortness of breath. She underwent cardiac catheterization, which showed stable coronary artery disease but critical aortic stenosis with a valve area of 0.8 cm² and mean gradient of 52 mmHg. Given her symptoms, she was referred to cardiothoracic surgery for evaluation of aortic valve replacement, either via surgical AVR or TAVR. Her kidney function remained stable, and she continued her home dialysis regimen. A mild post-procedural rise in white blood cell count was noted without signs of infection. She recovered well, was discharged home the following day, and instructed to follow up with surgery and primary care to monitor her condition and medications.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
